title: Genetic drift is strongest in small populations
caption: Six simulated populations each start with an allele at frequency 0.5 and change only by chance. With 20 gene copies the lines wander widely and some reach 0 (lost) or 1 (fixed); with 500 they stay close to 0.5. The simulation is seeded, so the picture does not change.
alt: Two panels of allele frequency against generation for six simulated populations each: with 20 gene copies the lines wander widely and some reach 0 or 1; with 500 gene copies they stay near 0.5.
description: Each line is one population, starting with the allele at frequency 0.5.
Every generation the alleles passed on are a random sample of those present: there is no selection.
N = 20: the frequencies wander far from 0.5, and some alleles are lost (0) or fixed (1) within 50 generations.
N = 500: the frequencies stay close to 0.5.
Drift is therefore strongest in small populations.
